audit.recode_to: Merge into kaqc1270 (Kaqchikel) as DUPLICATE, exactly as the sibling retired-code dialects kaqc1272/kaqc1276/kaqc1279 already were; same applies to kaqc1274 'Kaqchikel, Southern', which rests on the identical Berinstein quote. If a single Kaqchikel entry survives, its kind should be fixed-dominant (final) not fixed-strict: Bennett 2016:495 and ALMG 2004 document native non-final exceptions (janila, nana, tata, wakix, tukur) and penult-stressed Spanish loans; cite Rukemik 1997 Acento section / Bennett 2016 sec. 6.1 as deciding sources rather than Berinstein's background clause.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the three Berinstein 1979 passages exist verbatim at printed pp.47, vi, 52 (scanned of the open eScholarship scan fetched sources now; no copy was held before). (2) The deciding source is a 1979 MA-thesis perception experiment whose stress claim is a background premise about 'Cakchiquel' generically; its 46 subjects came from Patzicia, Chimaltenango (p.47), which Ethnologue 15 places in the Central [cak] area, not the Northern [ckc] San Martin Jilotepeque area. So the record attributes to Northern Kaqchikel a statement that is neither dialect-specific nor drawn from Northern speakers. sources.quote: p. 47: "To distinguish these hypotheses the perception experiment was repeated with speakers of Cakchiquel, a related Mayan language, which has fixed final stress and no phonemic length." Also abstract p. vi: "Both K'ekchi and Cakchiquel have fixed final stress but they differ in that while K'ekchi has phonemic vowel length, Cakchiquel does not." And p. 52: "the final syllable (the normal location of stress) will be longer than any other syllable in the word."
